design_decisions: Both public chart-edit entrypoints share plan_chart_edits and validate_splices. Validation preserves range-error precedence and sorting by start/end/planning sequence, but now finishes the overlap pass before any output.

The caller retains ownership of XML, scanned data, edit list and writer. The streaming path borrows unchanged byte slices and owns only planner replacement/structural fragments; it never builds a complete output buffer.

write_all implements short-write completion, Interrupted retry and WriteZero errors. Errors stop writing immediately; validation leaves the writer untouched, while I/O failure can leave a prefix. No flush or close is performed.

WritePatchError owns the original PatchError or io::Error and exposes it through Error::source. PatchError gains an additive Error implementation. Existing public signatures, fields, variants and exhaustive matching remain unchanged; only the new error enum is non-exhaustive.
Checked template lookup and slice access reject empty-series cloning and out-of-range template/index/order spans through existing PatchError variants instead of indexing panics.

Integration coverage exercises every ChartEdit variant, same-position append ordering, exact output parity, identity output, trait objects, borrowed input slices, late invalid/reversed/overlapping spans, structural overlaps, custom I/O payloads, prefix failures and no flush.
limitations: This is isolated component verification; no full document engine, rendering comparison, upstream integration or memory benchmark was run.
The API retains the existing requirement that ChartData describes the same XML. Planned replacement and structural fragments may allocate; no constant-memory guarantee is claimed.
No rollback is possible after an I/O failure; the caller must handle any prefix already written.
